newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to turn Banespa to federal bank.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to turn Banespa to federal bank.

text.p: Brazil's federal government will turn Sao Paulo state bank Banespa into a federal bank as a step towards possible privatization, Jornal do Brasil daily said on Monday.

The newspaper said the transformation of the bank into a federal institution was part of an agreement being negotiated between the Sao Paulo state and federal governments on a new restructuring plan for Sao Paulo's debt with Banespa.
Under the accord, Sao Paulo state government would pay off 20 percent of its 36.8 billion real debt to the bank with assets, Jornal do Brasil said.
Sao Paulo's state bank would have a private manager for one year, giving time for the federal government to decide whether it will be privatized or liquidated.
Because of Sao Paulo's massive debt to it, Banespa has been under Central Bank special temporary administration since December 1994.
The Central Bank management was initially for one year but was renewed for a further 12 months last December.
Earlier this year, Central Bank and Sao Paulo state government reached an accord on a restructuring plan for Sao Paulo's debt with Banespa, but this plan failed to make any progress.
